title: French Defense: the ideas
line: Black builds a solid pawn chain, then strikes at the base of White's center.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its king two squares, into the center.
Push the pawn in front of your king one square. It gets ready to back up a pawn on d5.

also.e7e5: That is the open game, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the French.
also.c7c5: That is the Sicilian Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the French.
also.c7c6: That is the Caro-Kann Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the French.
also.d7d6: That is the Pirc Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the French.
also.d7d5: That is the Scandinavian Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the French.
also.g7g6: That is the Modern Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the French.
also.g8f6: That is the Alekhine Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the French.

steps.text: Now push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It hits the pawn on e4, and your pawn on e6 guards it.
steps.after: White guards the pawn with a knight.

steps.text: The French has one drawback. Tap your bishop that the pawn on e6 shuts in.
steps.after: That bishop has few squares for now. Black frees it later, or trades it.

steps.text: Often White's pawn pushes past. The pawns lock into chains, and Black attacks White's chain at its base, the pawn on d4.
Push the pawn on c7 two squares to hit the base of the chain.

also.c8d7: That also works, and the bishop often goes there. This lesson hits the chain first.
also.g8e7: That also works. This lesson hits the chain first.

steps.after: White guards the base with another pawn.

steps.text: Bring the knight out. It is a second attacker on d4.

summary: Black's pawns build a solid chain. One bishop is shut in, and Black hits White's chain at its base.
